c2904.summary: Tyagaraja offers Rama the royal services — a jewelled umbrella, chamara whisks and a fragrant fan — fit only for him.
m: Accept these offerings of service, O you who recline on the king of serpents.
Clad in garments like ten million flashes of lightning, Lord of Janaki, have mercy —
you who direct the drama of illusion and grant the fruits we desire, Rama;
a golden umbrella set with countless gems — it befits only you.
Gleaming like lightning, with a golden handle,
a pair of chamaras bright as the autumn moon — they befit only you.
Fragrant with jasmine, champaka, marjoram and kuruveru,
a splendid fan — O one praised by Tyagaraja, it befits only you.

c2743.summary: An arati song: perform the protective rite for the Lord, Lakshmi's beloved, who loves music.
m: Perform the protective rite (arati) for the Lord,
for the beloved of Lakshmi, who shines on his chest;
for the Lord who shone holding Sita's hand; for the Lord who is won over
by Hanuman, son of the Wind; for the Lord whose arms protect Indra and the others;
for the Lord who loves music, sung by Tyagaraja, the lord of all glory.

c2890.summary: Does the mother come to the child, or the child go to the mother? Tyagaraja asks Rama to come to him.
m: Does the mother come to protect her child, or does the child go to the mother?
Best of the Solar race, explain this secret to me, and show me your face.
Does the cow follow the calf? Does the cloud go looking for the crops?
Does the lover go to the fish-eyed beloved? O one praised by Tyagaraja, come and tell me.

c2528.summary: Tyagaraja longs to see beautiful Rama to his eyes' content.
m: O beautiful Rama, let me see you to my eyes' content —
moon to the lily of Lakshmi's heart, incomparable one.
Your mind, your beauty, your splendour are unique — why harsh words, O God praised by Tyagaraja, divine one?

c1290.summary: A processional song: 'Come with care, Rama!' — describing Rama's jewels and the gods and devotees who receive him.
m: Come with care, O Ramachandra; come with care, O ocean of virtues,
father of Manmatha, protector of Indra.
As the gleam of your golden crown shines and your great earrings
sway, and your fine anklets jingle, Sanaka and the others rejoice to see you;
as strings of pearls sway, as attendants in two rows sing your praise, on the ruby
steps, slowly, listening to the veena's speech, enjoying the festivity —
as the parrot in the hand of your sister, come to see you, sings your glories to delight the mind,
as the gods shower flowers — come, brimming with charm, for great Tyagaraja to behold.

c2267.summary: Can such service be had? A rich picture of Vishnu on the swinging serpent bed, worshipped by gods and sages, and rocked by Tyagaraja.
m: Can such service be had?
Can even great Brahmins with little penance, or even the gods, obtain it?
As Tumburu and Narada sing kirtanas of his virtues with alapana, as Ambarisha and the foremost
chant his name and shower jasmine, as celestial women with bimba-red lips dance to flutes,
as Brahma, Indra and others on both sides praise his lineage and titles, as celestial
women wave fans, their bangles jingling, their jewelled necklaces swaying,
to see Hari reclining on the swinging serpent bed —
with golden robes shining on his emerald-hued body, the radiance
of the nails of his feet outshining young moons, his anklets gleaming, on his hands
diamond ornaments sparkling, on his chest pearl necklaces, and fine makara-shaped
earrings; his face with a gentle smile; curls; mirror-bright cheeks; lovely
the tilaka shining on his divine forehead — to behold the treasure of beauty on earth;
as sages free of dark qualities stand bewildered, unable to praise him enough,
as he holds court gracefully on the golden cradle — beholding Sita's lord, the granter of wishes,
overflowing with joy, Tyagaraja, son of Ramabrahmam, sings and rocks Rama,
uplifter of the world, terror of the gods' enemies, beyond the three gunas, all-fulfilled, pure consciousness,
abode of good qualities — to behold him to the eyes' content and in the heart.

c1106.summary: Rama is the support of Tyagaraja's life, the light of his eyes and the fruit of all his worship.
m: Support of my life, fruit of my vows,
lotus-eyed one, crown jewel of the kings of kings,
light of my sight, fragrance to my nose,
the form of the syllables of my japa, the flower of my daily worship, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2391.summary: Tyagaraja rejoices: today he has seen Sri Rama, served by his brothers, Hanuman and Sugriva.
m: I have seen Sri Rama today — my wish fulfilled to my eyes' content.
Sita's lord, born gracefully in the Solar race on this earth — today,
as Bharata, Lakshmana and Shatrughna serve him, as the Wind's son holds his feet,
as Sugriva and the brave chiefs praise him — the one praised by Tyagaraja, today.

c2362.summary: What bliss could be greater than losing oneself in singing of Rama until one becomes one with him?
m: What bliss is there greater than this, O Rama, Rama —
the bliss that all true saints agree upon?
Dancing, singing in nada, weeping and pleading, staying united with you in the mind — that is enough.
Through singing Sri Hari's praise, forgetting body and senses, becoming 'I am He' — that is enough.
When I chant you, the worlds themselves shine as you, O one of glorious story, praised by Tyagaraja.

c2619.summary: Tyagaraja reflects that his suffering is the fruit of past-life misdeeds, and wonders whether the Name can still prevail.
m: I have come to know the mischief I did in a past birth, Rama.
Its result is plain — does a sore on one's palm need a mirror to be seen?
Can a fine paddy shoot flourish among millet plants?
O one reclining on the serpent, can the merit of the Name shine through Tyagaraja's sins?

c1403.summary: Why won't Rama show mercy? This is no time for indifference — followed by a cascade of epithets in praise of Rama.
m: Why won't your mercy come? This is not the time for indifference.
Clad in pure gold, protector of the good, beloved of Lakshmi, bearer of arrows,
giver of good, abode of compassion, dark as a rain cloud, wearing a fresh forest garland — (why?)
Come, God of gods! Come, great one! Come, lotus-eyed son of the Raghus!
Heart full of the finest nectar, deep as the ocean, surrounded by kin, slayer of demons,
tender as Manmatha, who dwells among the wise, essence of all the Vedas — (show mercy) on me.
King of kings, whose feet the sages worship, with eyes like the sun, refuge of all, most beautiful,
praised by Shiva, rider of Garuda, whose feet Indra worships, father of Brahma,
radiant as ten million suns, a lion to the herds of demon elephants, lotus-faced,
protector of the sacrifice, worshipped by great devotees, held in the hearts of great yogis, without beginning
or end, reclining on the serpent, giver of boons to the elephant king, wearing punnaga flowers, ever
the remover of sin, whose feet the Wind's son holds, abiding at the end of the Vedas, free of attachment, praised by Sri Tyagaraja.

c2350.summary: Addressed to Shiva of Tiruvaiyaru: who named you 'remover of the sorrows of those who bow', if you show me no mercy?
m: Who on earth gave you the name 'remover of the sorrows of those who bow', Shankara?
I have long thought of you, melted, and prostrated before you — have you no mercy on me?
Did I not bow down with hands, feet, forehead and arms touching the ground?
Did I not cry out 'refuge'? O Lord of Panchanada, praised by Tyagaraja — (who named you so)?

c1393.summary: After recounting Rama's labours — the forest, the deer, Ravana, Lanka — Tyagaraja invites him to rest.
m: Lie down and rest, so your weariness may pass.
You have cut away unrelenting sins, O emperor, Rama of Saketa.
Seeing Brahma's distress, you shone forth as lord of the Solar race, went to the forest with lotus-eyed Sita,
slew the deer, crushed wicked Ravana's pride, and to fearless Vibhishana
gave golden Lanka and protected the gods — O spotless one, Rama praised by Tyagaraja.

c2520.summary: Don't leave me, Rama: finding you is like shade in scorching heat, a pearl from the deep sea, or buried treasure.
m: Don't leave me and go away —
Ramayya, don't leave me.
Apart from you
I cannot bear even a moment.
It is like finding, in unbearable summer heat,
the shade of the wish-fulfilling tree — at this moment;
like diving into the sea, holding one's breath,
and finding a flawless pearl, O Lord of Lakshmi;
like digging deep into the earth
and finding a pot of treasure — so I found you, (I your) servant;
like, when heatstroke strikes, great
cool hailstones pouring down — at this moment.
Rule over me well, O
one praised by Tyagaraja — this body is yours.

c1077.summary: Tyagaraja's garland of a hundred ragas (songs), in which Hari delights — a jewel to cross the ocean of life.
m: Hari delights in the jewelled garland of ragas, (these hundred songs).
Come, let us serve him well and attain all good fortune.
It is the true path, carrying the meaning of the Vedas, six Shastras, Puranas and Agamas, in which great yogis find bliss;
they are kirtanas sung by great devotees together — the hundred songs Tyagaraja made as a jewel to cross over.

c2268.summary: Tyagaraja asks the all-witnessing Consciousness: is duality bliss, or non-duality?
m: Is duality bliss, or is non-duality bliss?
O Consciousness, witness of all, listen, and tell me fully.
In the sky, wind, sun, earth and the rest, in Shiva, Indra and the gods, and the lord of mountains,
in the foremost devotees of the Lord — you who delight in them all, worshipped by Tyagaraja.
Lullaby, Rama, cloud of bliss.
Lullaby, Rama, child of Dasharatha; lullaby, Rama, beloved of the Earth's daughter.
Lullaby, Rama, jewel of the Raghu race; lullaby, Rama of curly locks.
Lullaby, Rama, beyond attributes; lullaby, Rama, wish-tree of virtues.
Lullaby, Rama, with the sun and moon for eyes; lullaby, Rama reclining on the serpent king.
Lullaby, Rama of gentle speech; lullaby, Rama of lovely attire.
Lullaby, Rama worshipped by Tyagaraja; lullaby, Rama, beloved of the devotees.

c2825.summary: Without peace of mind there is no happiness — not even for those with family, wealth, learning or ritual merit.
m: Without peace of mind there is no happiness, O lotus-eyed one,
even for the self-controlled, even for a master of Vedanta.
Though one has wife, children, wealth and grain, though one has the riches of japa and penance,
though one has studied all the Agamas and Shastras, though one knows well the feelings of every heart,
though one has performed every ritual such as sacrifices, though one is well known as a devotee —
O king of kings, Sri Raghava, praised by Tyagaraja, protector of the good — (there is no happiness without peace).

c2538.summary: Why should we worry? Rama holds the strings of the world's puppet-play and makes all dance in step.
m: Why should we worry, O Sri Ramachandra, our refuge?
Prince of Saketa, wish-tree to true devotees, bestower of fortune!
Gathering all together, holding the strings of the puppet-play in your hand as the world admires,
you make them dance without missing a step — praised by Tyagaraja who bows to you, and by Shiva.

c1505.summary: Whom did the great ones take you to be — Shiva, Vishnu, Brahma or the Supreme? 'Rama' holds the life of both the Shiva and Narayana mantras.
m: Whom did the great men decide you to be? How did they worship you?
As Shiva, as Madhava, as lotus-born Brahma, or as the Supreme Brahman?
'Ma' is the life of the Shiva mantra; 'Ra' is the life of the Madhava mantra —
I bow to the great ones who know this secret, O generous one praised by Tyagaraja.

c1339.summary: Who is truly happy? The one who lives by truth, serves all, sees no difference among gods, and sings Rama's name.
m: Who is truly happy? Who is happy in Rama's name?
Who is happy, who is blessed — through the saving name, the essence of all?
One who never swerves from truth, serves all beings, and sees no difference among gods,
and who always sings with eternal, tuneful music — O Rama praised by Tyagaraja.

c2839.summary: A hymn to the sage Narada, master of the veena and of nada.
m: O Sri Narada, bee to the lotus of nada, of auspicious form,
protector of the honour of the lowly, (dear to) the Lord of the world,
master of the truth of playing the noble veena born of the Vedas, free of the three afflictions, praised by the celestials,
dear friend of the one born in the Yadava clan, ever joyful, best of sages, bestower of fortune, praised by Tyagaraja — protect me.

c2716.summary: Understand how the Supreme Self shines in everything — in gods and men, the elements, all creatures, the good and the bad.
m: Understand well the wonder of how the Supreme Self shines.
Whether Hari or Hara, gods or men, or countless universes — in all of them,
in sky, wind, fire, water and earth, in countless beasts, birds, mountains and trees,
in the virtuous and the wicked, and always in Tyagaraja and all who seek refuge.

c1388.summary: How great is devotion to Rama! Without it, would Sita, Lakshmana, Bharata, Shabari or Hanuman have done what they did?
m: Ah! How great is devotion to Rama!
It ends our wanderings and guards us as the eyelid guards the eye.
(Without it) would Lakshmi love him? Would Lakshmana serve him?
Would subtle-minded Bharata gaze and gaze at him and swoon?
Would Shabari offer him fruit she had tasted? Would Shiva, who wears the moon, praise him?
Would God grant the ascetic Svayamprabha the immovable state?
Would a monkey cross the ocean? Would (Krishna) let a cowherd girl tie him to a mortar?
Would the sinner Tyagaraja's bliss keep growing?
